# Mohith Rai Srivastav

> Architectural photographer, filmmaker, and educator based in Goa, India. Architect by education, photographer by practice.

## About

Mohith Rai Srivastav translates the built environment through a practice of slowness, materiality, and sustained attention. His work spans architectural photography, slow cinema, and fine art prints. He is based in Goa, India, and works across South Asia.

## What This Site Offers

### Fine Art Prints (Shop)
Limited-edition archival pigment prints on 310 GSM etching rag. Each print is signed, numbered, and accompanied by a certificate of authenticity. Nine works are currently available, from the Resurface series. Every print is offered in multiple sizes (Small, Medium, Standard, Large) with the Standard and Large formats as the flagship editions. Custom larger formats are available on request for collectors, galleries, and institutional spaces. Prints ship worldwide, fully insured. Prices range from INR 55,000 to INR 1,25,000 depending on size and edition. The shop includes augmented reality (AR) preview — buyers can place prints on their wall using their phone camera before purchasing.

### Resurface (Photographic Series)
An ongoing photographic enquiry into how the built world remains active through surface, erosion, and light. Each chapter explores different material conditions, climates, and qualities of light. Chapter I was exhibited at the Goa Open Arts Festival 2026. Prints are produced on archival etching rag without glass framing.

### Creative Workshops — Lived Space
A hands-on creative observation workshop based in Goa, India — and available on invitation nationwide and internationally. The workshop places observation first — participants spend time in the field noticing people, routines, and sensory detail, then take a single constraint and respond in their own medium. The practice changes how you choose and what you make. Institutions, design schools, festivals, and organizations can invite Lived Space to their city.

**Method:** Three repeatable steps — (1) Observe: no camera, no notebook, just look. (2) Constrain: one card, one instruction, work inside it completely. (3) Make: one response in your medium. The depth comes from how you apply them.

**Open to:** Photographers, architects, writers, filmmakers, musicians, designers — any creative discipline. Beginner to professional. No prior experience required.

**Formats:**
- The One-Day Immersion — 6 to 8 hours, one completed work in your medium. INR 3,600. 2026–2027 dates: 2 July 2026, 9 August 2026, 2 September 2026, 9 November 2026, 5 December 2026, 1 February 2027, 3 March 2027.
- The Three-Day Intensive — Three days of fieldwork, constraint exercises, and group critique across multiple spaces. INR 11,400. 2026–2027 start dates: 6 July 2026, 5 August 2026, 4 September 2026, 11 November 2026, 6 December 2026, 3 February 2027, 5 March 2027.
- The Seven-Day Residency — A full-week creative residency closing with one finished work. INR 24,000. 2026–2027 start dates: 1 October 2026, 9 January 2027, 1 April 2027.
- All sessions held in Goa, India. Capped at 12 people each.

**Includes:** All workshop sessions, Explorer's Deck (constraint cards), field guidance during observation, group review after every session.
**Not included:** Travel, accommodation, meals, personal equipment.
**What to bring:** Your medium, comfortable clothing for extended time outdoors, a willingness to observe before you make.

**Takeaway:** Participants learn to observe a space across multiple sensory layers with intention, identify the gap between design intent and lived use, use a chosen medium as a focusing constraint for inquiry, synthesize individual observations into a collective narrative, and articulate design thinking that comes from observation. These outcomes feed directly into studio work, site analysis, case studies, design briefs, and juries — and apply equally to any creative professional working across space, material, and human behaviour.

### Teaching & Institutional Engagements

Mohith Rai Srivastav works as a Workshop Tutor and educator at architecture schools, student conventions, and creative institutions across India.

**Institutional Record:**
- NASA India — 68th Annual Convention (June 2026): Invited to conduct Lived Space: Creative Observation at Woxsen School of Architecture & Planning, Hyderabad. NASA India is the National Association of Students of Architecture, representing 66,000 students across 350+ colleges.
- CARE School of Architecture, Trichy (2024): Workshop on Photography as a Tool for Architects, co-facilitated with Bharath Ramamrutham.
- ASTU-AAS Webinar (2023): Architectural Photography — Discussion & Insight, hosted by the Association of Architecture Students, Adama Science and Technology University, Ethiopia. International engagement.

### Architectural Photography Services
Available for architectural documentation, editorial work, and bespoke print commissions worldwide. Major clientele includes architects, interior designers, industrial designers, landscape designers, luxury hospitality brands (hotels and resorts), commercial offices, and institutions. Portfolio spans residential, institutional, heritage, and hospitality projects across India (Goa, Karnataka, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Punjab, Rajasthan, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Delhi NCR, Chandigarh, Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad) and internationally (United States, United Kingdom, UAE, Singapore, Australia, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Portugal, Japan, Canada, Netherlands, Switzerland, Thailand, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Maldives). Based in Goa, India — working globally.

### Fine Art & Exhibitions
Mohith's work sits at the intersection of architecture and fine art. His prints are collected by art collectors, curators, and institutional buyers. He is open to gallery exhibitions, art residencies, museum shows, art fairs, and curatorial collaborations. Previous exhibition: Goa Open Arts Festival 2026. Available for artist residencies, group and solo exhibitions, and commissioned installations for public and private spaces.

### Journal & Essays
Long-form essays on architectural photography, light, time, observation, materiality, and the gap between what architects draw and what people experience. Written from years of working inside finished buildings across India and South Asia.

**Currently published:**
- "What Architectural Photography Taught Me About Space" (May 2026) — On planning a shoot around the sun path, what changes between the recce and the shoot day, and what years of photographing finished buildings has taught about light, time, use, and the gap between what is drawn and what is experienced. https://www.mohithraisrivastav.com/what-architectural-photography-taught-me-about-space.html

The full journal index lives at https://www.mohithraisrivastav.com/blog.html and updates with new field notes and essays.
